sections.history: Thirupoonthuruthi lies south of the Kaveri, a short way south-west of Thiruvaiyaru, and its name speaks of a flowering islet among the streams of the delta. The temple is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, sung by Appar and Sambandar in the Tevaram, and it holds a special place in the life of Appar. He is remembered as having settled here, founding a matha and serving the temple with his own hands, clearing its courtyards in the humble service known as uzhavarappani. The village is often called Mela Thirupoonthuruthi, to set it apart from its neighbour.
sections.architecture: The temple is a Dravidian stone shrine of the delta, with the sanctum of Pushpavananathar at its heart and a separate shrine for the goddess Soundaryanayaki, whose name means the lady of beauty. Its walls and mandapams have been extended and renewed over the centuries. For pilgrims the most treasured spaces are the open courts where Appar is believed to have laboured, and the approach outside the temple where, tradition says, Sambandar chose to stand in worship rather than tread on ground the older saint had hallowed.
sections.legends: Two stories meet here. Indra, bearing a curse, is said to have worshipped Shiva at this place with flowers, and so the lord is Pushpavananathar, lord of the flower grove. The second is the tender meeting of the two Tevaram saints. When the young Sambandar came in his palanquin to see Appar, the aged saint quietly joined the bearers. Sambandar asked where Appar was, and a voice from beneath the palanquin answered that he was there, carrying it; the two saints then bowed at each other's feet.
sections.festivals: In the Saptha Sthanam festival of Chithirai (April–May), Thirupoonthuruthi is the sixth temple of the round, reached after Thirukandiyur. Tradition holds that its flower groves supplied the garlands for Nandi's wedding, and the temple still sends flowers to the yearly celebration of that wedding. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are also observed. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thirupoonthuruthi is a place for those who love the Tevaram saints. Walk the courtyard slowly, remembering the old man who once swept it clean, and pause at the entrance where the younger saint is said to have stood in reverence. It is a quiet village temple, easily reached from Thirukandiyur and Thiruvaiyaru, and a bunch of flowers is a fitting offering here.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but strictly prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Thirupoonthuruthi lies about 4 km south-west of Thiruvaiyaru and some 12 km from Thanjavur, reached by local roads from either town; an auto or taxi is the easiest way to come. Thanjavur is the nearest major railway station, and Tiruchirappalli International Airport, about 55 km away, is the nearest airport.
